result:
Based on my thorough analysis of the Dog orchestrator source code (1893 lines of Python) and the architectural documentation, I can now provide a comprehensive prompt engineering analysis. Note that Conductor appears to be a conceptual meta-orchestrator mentioned in documentation but not actually implemented as a separate codebase.

```json
{
  "architectural_implications": [
    "Multi-layer prompt assembly architecture (specialists + teams + workflows) creates composable, reusable prompt templates that enable consistent prompt engineering patterns across workflows",
    "File substitution mechanism ({{ filename.json }}) in prompts enables sophisticated data flow between workflow stages, allowing prompts to dynamically incorporate previous LLM outputs for iterative refinement",
    "Team tone injection provides conversation context layer that shapes LLM response style without requiring per-block prompt tuning, enabling prompt standardization",
    "Logic phase architecture (pre/post/validate/custom) separates prompt engineering from data preprocessing/validation, allowing prompt engineers to focus on LLM interaction quality while logic scripts handle data transformation",
    "Specialist MD file format enables version-controlled, reusable system prompt fragments that can be composed into complex multi-role prompts without duplication",
    "Dual API support (Anthropic + OpenRouter) creates prompt portability concerns - prompts designed for Claude Opus 4.5 may behave differently on other models accessed via OpenRouter",
    "Task-based directory isolation (tasks/<id>/outputs/) enables reproducible prompt testing by preserving input-output pairs and allowing prompt iteration without cross-contamination",
    "Dependency graph (depends_on) enables multi-stage reasoning workflows where later prompts build on earlier LLM outputs, supporting chain-of-thought and critique-revision patterns",
    "Environment variable-based configuration (.env files per flow) allows prompt customization (MAX_TOKENS, TEMPERATURE) without modifying YAML, enabling prompt tuning experimentation",
    "Workflow resumability via SQLite state enables long-running multi-stage prompt workflows with human-in-the-loop review points, critical for complex reasoning tasks"
  ],
  
  "qa_implications": [
    "Zero test coverage (0%) means prompt engineering changes have no automated validation - prompt regressions cannot be detected without manual review of LLM outputs",
    "No retry logic means transient API failures cause prompt execution to fail permanently, requiring manual workflow restart and losing partial results",
    "File substitution errors fail silently in some cases (dog.py:412 logs warning but continues) - prompts may receive incomplete data without explicit failure, producing hallucinated or invalid LLM responses",
    "Thread-safety gaps in completed dict (dog.py:133) create race conditions in multi-threaded execution - dependency resolution may incorrectly trigger blocks before dependencies complete, feeding incomplete data to prompts",
    "No prompt output validation beyond file existence check - LLM may produce malformed JSON or incomplete responses that pass validation, breaking downstream prompt stages",
    "Lack of circuit breaker for API calls means repeated prompt failures (e.g., rate limits, model errors) cascade through workflow without backoff, wasting API credits",
    "No structured logging of prompt inputs/outputs beyond dog.log makes prompt debugging difficult - cannot easily correlate prompt variations with output quality",
    "Timeout enforcement at workflow level only (not per-block) means stuck LLM calls block semaphore slots indefinitely, causing workflow deadlock",
    "No versioning of specialist/team/flow definitions means prompt changes affect in-flight workflows unpredictably, breaking reproducibility",
    "Validation engine integration (Phase 1) is optional and continues on error (dog.py:309) - invalid workflow schemas may execute with unexpected prompt assembly behavior"
  ],
  
  "recommendations": [
    "Implement prompt output schema validation using Pydantic or JSON Schema to catch malformed LLM responses immediately, preventing cascade failures in multi-stage workflows",
    "Add prompt versioning metadata to task.json (specialist versions, team version, flow version) to enable reproducibility and A/B testing of prompt variations",
    "Create prompt test harness using task system - define golden input/output pairs for critical flows, run regression tests on prompt changes to detect quality degradation",
    "Implement retry logic with exponential backoff specifically for API calls (dog.py:429-481), with configurable max retries per block to handle transient failures gracefully",
    "Add structured prompt/response logging to separate JSON files (tasks/<id>/prompts/<stage>.json containing {prompt, response, metadata}) for prompt engineering analysis",
    "Build prompt template validation pre-flight checks: detect undefined file substitutions ({{ missing.json }}), validate specialist references exist, check team/specialist compatibility",
    "Implement thread-safe state management using proper locking around completed set and processes dict to eliminate race conditions in dependency resolution",
    "Add per-block timeout configuration (timeout_seconds field in block YAML) to prevent hung API calls from blocking workflow progress",
    "Create prompt performance metrics collection: track token usage, latency, cost per block and save to task metadata for prompt optimization analysis",
    "Implement prompt caching mechanism: hash (specialist + team + prompt template) and cache responses for deterministic prompts to reduce API costs during development/testing",
    "Add LLM response quality scoring integration: call validation logic phase with LLM output, score quality 0-100, retry with modified prompt if below threshold",
    "Build prompt template IDE support: create JSON schema for workflow YAML v2.5.3 to enable autocomplete/validation in VSCode when editing flows",
    "Implement prompt A/B testing framework: support variants field in blocks allowing multiple specialist/prompt combinations, execute both, compare outputs",
    "Add human-in-the-loop prompt refinement: pause workflow after stage, present LLM output for review, allow prompt editing and re-execution before continuing",
    "Create prompt library analytics: track which specialists/teams/flows are used most, identify reusable patterns, refactor duplicated prompt fragments into shared specialists"
  ]
}
```

Анализ основан на детальном изучении исходного кода Dog (1893 строки Python, включая классы Process, DogState, ProcessManager, DogUI) и архитектурной документации. Dog представляет собой зрелую систему оркестрации с многослойной архитектурой промптов (specialists → teams → workflows), но имеет критические пробелы в QA (0% покрытие тестами, отсутствие retry логики, проблемы с thread-safety), которые непосредственно влияют на надёжность prompt engineering workflows.

Ключевые находки:
1. Архитектура промптов высокого качества с композируемыми слоями, но без версионирования и валидации
2. Продвинутый data flow через file substitution, но с silent failures
3. Критические QA пробелы делают prompt workflows хрупкими для production использования

Conductor существует только как концептуальный мета-оркестратор в документации, реальной кодовой базы не обнаружено.
